result_expr: Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*rho_v(x, y, z, t), t) + rho_i*Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), t) - Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*D(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), x), x) - Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*D(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), y), y) - Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*D(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), z), z)

symbols.name: rho_i
symbols.meaning: density of ice, taken as constant

symbols.name: D(T)
symbols.meaning: diffusivity of water vapor in the pore gas

steps.statement: Water mass per unit total volume: m = rho_i*phi + (1-phi)*rho_v [kg m^-3]
steps.operation: Volume-fraction weighting of the ice and gas phases

steps.statement: d/dt ∫_V m dV = -∮ J·n dA for any fixed V, so d_t m + div J = 0
steps.operation: Conservation of water mass, then the divergence theorem with V arbitrary

steps.statement: J = -(1-phi) D(T) grad rho_v (ice is stationary; Fickian diffusion through the gas fraction only) [kg m^-2 s^-1]
d_t[(1-phi) rho_v] + rho_i d_t phi - div[(1-phi) D(T) grad rho_v] = 0; rho_i d_t phi is the ice-vapor exchange term (checked with SymPy and pint in scratch/check.py)
steps.operation: Substitute S1 and S3 into S2, with rho_i constant

steps.statement: Equivalent form: (1-phi) d_t rho_v + (rho_i - rho_v) d_t phi - div[(1-phi) D grad rho_v] = 0 (checked with SymPy)
R = d_t[(1-phi) rho_v] + rho_i d_t phi - sum over x, y, z of d_xi[(1-phi) D(T) d_xi rho_v] = 0
steps.operation: Write the divergence in 3D Cartesian coordinates

assumptions_used: phi and T are known, smooth fields (given)
Ice is rigid and does not move; the ice density rho_i is constant (needed in S4)
Vapor moves only by Fickian diffusion through the gas fraction, so the flux is weighted by (1-phi); D may depend on T
No bulk gas flow, and no water sources or sinks other than ice-vapor phase change
Water mass is m = rho_i*phi + (1-phi)*rho_v (volume-fraction mixture)

neglected.effect: Thermal expansion of ice (rho_i depending on T)
neglected.why: The volumetric expansion coefficient is about 1.5e-4 K^-1, so rho_i changes by less than 1% over tens of K

neglected.effect: Advection by bulk gas flow, including Stefan flow
neglected.why: Near 200 K the vapor mole fraction is about 1e-6 to 1e-5, so the flow that sublimation drives is negligible next to diffusion
The thermal diffusion factor of water in air is about 0.1 or less, so the term is a small correction to the flux driven by concentration gradients

neglected.effect: Adsorption on regolith grains and grain motion
neglected.why: Outside this model of the pore space; the grains are treated as inert boundaries
Folded into the effective D(T); if it matters, D would also depend on pore size
